title: Find a simpler initialisation pattern
body:
Current implementation:

``` js
var instant = new instantSearch.InstantSearch(appId, apiKey, indexName);
```

Most of our libraries are using:

``` js
var instance = someFunction(appId, apiKey);
```

It could be good to have the same pattern? @redox @pixelastic @bobylito

comments.body: Yep, I'd rather have a `var instance = instantSearch(foo, bar)`. Not sure if we need to pass the indexName when creating the instance or later (do we handle search in multiple indices at once?)

> Yep, I'd rather have a var instance = instantSearch(foo, bar). Not sure if we need to pass the indexName when creating the instance or later (do we handle search in multiple indices at once?)

We do need at least one indexName since one instant search interface is always targeting an index.

Then some widgets like sortOrder (sort by popularity, price ..) will need to use other indexes but it's in their APIs.

Honestly I would be a bit surprised by this kind of API.

Documentation tooling aside, given our previous modules, I would advocate for something like:

``` js
var instantsearch = require('instantsearch');
var search = instantsearch(appId, apiKey, indexName);
```

I know @bobylito this is not what you prefer, adding it because I feel this is straightforward.
